common_name: Kindly Light Daylily (Historic Narrow Spider-Form Yellow Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Kindly Light is a historic true spider-form daylily introduced in 1950, its narrow, twisted yellow petals among the earliest examples of the spider form.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Kindly Light, introduced in 1950 by daylily breeder Ezra Kraus, bears narrow, dramatically twisted and recurved yellow petals that helped define the true spider form of daylily flowers, a shape distinct from the broader, rounder blooms typical of most mid-century cultivars. Its long, spidery petals and vigorous, floriferous habit have kept it in cultivation for over seventy years as a historically significant parent behind many modern spider and unusual-form daylily hybrids. Divide every three to four years when bloom declines, and deadhead spent scapes to keep the planting tidy.

common_name: Little Business Daylily (Miniature Wine-Red Floriferous Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Little Business is a compact, extremely floriferous miniature daylily with wine-red flowers, excellent for edging and containers.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Little Business bears small, rounded, wine-red flowers with a bright green throat on a compact plant that produces an unusually high number of branches and buds per scape, giving it one of the longest and most prolific bloom displays of any widely grown miniature daylily. Its small stature and heavy flowering make it a favorite for edging paths, containers, and the front of a mixed border where larger daylily cultivars would overwhelm the space. Divide every three to four years when bloom declines, and deadhead spent scapes to keep the planting tidy.

common_name: Moonlit Masquerade Daylily (Lavender-Purple with Cream Appliqué Band Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Moonlit Masquerade won the American Hemerocallis Society Stout Silver Medal in 2008 for its lavender-purple petals edged in a wide cream-white band.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun. Moonlit Masquerade bears lavender-purple petals bordered by a wide, distinct cream-white edge often described as an appliqué band, a striking two-tone pattern that earned it the American Hemerocallis Society's Stout Silver Medal in 2008, the organization's highest honor for a daylily cultivar. Its large, ruffled blooms open over a long summer season on well-branched scapes carrying a high bud count for extended flowering. Divide every three to four years when bloom declines, and deadhead spent scapes to keep the planting tidy.
sources: American Hemerocallis Society — Stout Silver Medal
